items.title: Meet Martini: a 'film set' for AI video that gives filmmakers real cinematic controls
items.excerpt: Martini is a new collaborative, web-based platform pitched as a virtual 'film set' for both AI and non-AI video production, letting users compose shots in 2D or 3D environments with actual cinematic controls across multiple AI video models rather than gambling on 'prompt roulette.' It's out now with a free plan for indie filmmakers.

items.title: “I Spent 15 Years Making Movies the Old Way. Now I’m, Reluctantly, an AI Guy”
items.excerpt: A producer with 15 years of traditional moviemaking experience walks through his shift to generative-AI tools in pre- and post-production, arguing that folding AI into the workflow can lower costs and democratize filmmaking rather than replace human creativity — a first-person view of how AI is reshaping a working film craftsperson's pipeline.

items.title: AI feature 'Gods Don't Give Gifts' poised to make the leap from YouTube to the big screen
items.excerpt: 'Gods Don't Give Gifts,' a fully AI-generated feature from the Gossip Goblin channel, is set to become the next AI film to jump from a large YouTube following to theatrical release — a concrete case study in generative-AI filmmaking reaching mainstream distribution.

items.title: Venice-set Reply AI Film Festival unveils finalists and jury
items.excerpt: The third Reply AI Film Festival, running alongside the Venice Film Festival, picked 10 AI-made shorts from 3,000 submissions across 76 countries and named a jury including Gabriele Salvatores, Catherine Hardwicke and Jed Weintrob. Winners for Best Short Film, an AI for Good Award and the Reply AI Studios Grand Prix will be announced September 6.

items.title: Reply AI Film Festival reveals jury: Rob Minkoff, Catherine Hardwicke
items.excerpt: Variety reports the Venice-adjacent Reply AI Film Festival for AI-made shorts has revealed its jury, including 'The Lion King' director Rob Minkoff and 'Twilight' director Catherine Hardwicke, ahead of its winners announcement — a marker of established filmmakers engaging with generative-AI short-film craft. (Same festival as the Deadline item; kept for outlet diversity.)
